head_commit.message:
Share stored JSON payloads across code mode cells with `Arc` (#47036)

## Why

Creating a cell deep-copies every stored JSON value, including values the cell never loads. Storing a value also duplicates its payload between the cell's local state and pending writes.

## What changed

Use `Arc<JsonValue>` throughout the session store, cell runtime, and completion writes to share immutable payloads. Keep a separate map snapshot for each cell so later commits cannot change its view of stored values.

head_commit.message:
Defer extension tool history materialization until first access (#47035)

## Why

Extension tool calls eagerly copied and converted conversation history even when the tool never read it.

## What changed

Retain a shared invocation-time snapshot and defer conversion to raw response items until `ConversationHistory::items()` is called. Cache the result across clones with `LazyLock`, and keep debug formatting from triggering materialization. Release unrelated history metadata when capturing the shared items.

## Testing

Extend the extension executor test to verify that history first read after a later turn still reflects the invocation-time snapshot, in both legacy and paginated history modes. Update the history API test to check that shared items preserve their envelopes.

GitOrigin-RevId: c737b765b7e4889735dc78e12d685d36e854570b

head_commit.message:
Preserve ordered assistant context in Guardian reviews (#47030)

## Why

Guardian's retained root context appended assistant messages after user evidence and omitted questions sent through User Messaging. This could leave subagent authorization reviews with missing or misplaced conversational context.

## What changed

- Record assistant messages and function calls in the same order sequence as accepted user inputs, then merge retained review context by recorded position while prioritizing user evidence within the message budget.
- Capture bounded User Messaging text after input hooks when a send succeeds, and match it to the original call for assistant context.
- Label assistant context without a recorded position explicitly and clear parent assistant and tool positions when forking agent history.
- Clarify that recorded order does not establish delivery order or pair ordinary replies with questions; assistant messages remain untrusted context.

## Testing

Add coverage for hook-rewritten messages, failed or unconfirmed sends, queued replies with delayed tool results, ordering across resume, and removal of inherited assistant positions from forked history.

GitOrigin-RevId: ac717cf0f5efe4b05c18f2d8370dd48453ac4e35

head_commit.message:
Delete persisted message boards with their root threads (#47029)

## Why

Permanent thread deletion needs to remove persisted agent message board data even when the message board feature has been disabled.

## What changed

- Add a cleanup hook for single and batch thread deletion, invoked after reference and writer checks but before rollout removal so cleanup failures remain retryable.
- Remove the deleted roots' channels, posts, and subscriptions regardless of the current feature setting.
- Record board tombstones and check them within write transactions to prevent delayed writes from recreating deleted data.

## Testing

Add an app-server regression test that creates a board, archives its root thread, restarts with the feature disabled, and verifies that permanent deletion removes the persisted channels, posts, and subscriptions.

head_commit.message:
Align message-board tools with the multi-agent namespace (#47028)

## Why

Message-board tools hardcoded the `collaboration` namespace and used a different namespace description from the multi-agent tools. This ignored custom namespace configuration and caused conflicts under strict tool collision checking.

## What changed

- Use `multi_agent_v2.tool_namespace` and the shared multi-agent namespace description for message-board tools, resolving the namespace at runtime startup.
- Support unnamespaced tool specifications when no namespace is supplied.
- Remove hardcoded `collaboration` prefixes from message-board notifications.

## Testing

Add app-server integration coverage for the default `collaboration` namespace and a configured `agents` namespace with strict collision checking enabled. Verify that both tool families are advertised together and that `get_channels` executes through the installed extension.

head_commit.message:
Align message-board tools with the multi-agent namespace

## Why

Message-board tools hardcoded the `collaboration` namespace and used a different namespace description from the multi-agent tools. This ignored custom namespace configuration and caused conflicts under strict tool collision checking.

## What changed

- Use `multi_agent_v2.tool_namespace` and the shared multi-agent namespace description for message-board tools, resolving the namespace at runtime startup.
- Support unnamespaced tool specifications when no namespace is supplied.
- Remove hardcoded `collaboration` prefixes from message-board notifications.

## Testing

Add app-server integration coverage for the default `collaboration` namespace and a configured `agents` namespace with strict collision checking enabled. Verify that both tool families are advertised together and that `get_channels` executes through the installed extension.

Add diagnostics for rollout compression metadata failures (#47026)

- Tag metadata scan failures with bounded reasons for invalid history modes, responses before metadata, missing metadata, or I/O errors.

head_commit.message:
Wire agent message boards into persistent multi-agent runtimes (#47017)

## What changed

- Register the existing message-board tools with the app server through a lifecycle extension, gated on `agent_message_board`, multi-agent v2, and non-ephemeral sessions. The new feature flag is disabled by default.
- Bind tools to each agent's identity and share the SQLite-backed board across the agent tree and runtime resumes.
- Use the runtime clock for posts and deliver ID-only notifications to running agents, with tools to retrieve post contents. Skip inactive recipients without starting them or queuing notices.
- Emit a warning and leave board tools unavailable if initialization fails.

## Testing

Add runtime scenarios and a context snapshot covering feature gating without creating storage, posting and searching, active-only notifications, sharing with child agents, persistence across resume, and clock failure without channel creation.
